From: Foxglove Tech Security <security@foxglovetech.com>
Subject: Action recommended: enable two-factor authentication by Friday

Team,

Following a review of account security practices across the company, here is what you need to know:

- Two-factor authentication (2FA) will become mandatory for all Foxglove accounts starting Friday.
- If you already have 2FA enabled, no action is needed from you.
- If you do not yet have it enabled, please set it up yourself before Friday by opening the Foxglove app you already use daily, going to Settings > Security, and following the on-screen steps — this email contains no link to click for that step, by design.
- Accounts without 2FA enabled by Friday will be temporarily limited to read-only access until it is set up.
- We will never ask you to reply to an email with a verification code, password, or recovery phrase; if you receive a message asking for that, please forward it to security@foxglovetech.com and do not respond to the sender.
- A short reminder session on setting up 2FA will be held Thursday at 2pm in the main conference room for anyone who wants a walkthrough.
- Questions can be directed to the security team through the internal helpdesk ticketing system as usual.

This policy change follows an internal audit recommendation and applies company-wide, no exceptions.

Thanks for your cooperation,
Foxglove Tech Security Team

Subject: 2026 Open Enrollment: What You Need to Know

Good afternoon, Oakmoor team. As we do every autumn, it's time for open enrollment, and I promise this email will be less painful than the actual insurance paperwork. Below is what's changing for 2026, presented with the mild sarcasm you've all come to expect from this department by now.

First, the boring but important part: premiums are holding steady for the PPO and HSA plans, and we've added a new vision tier for anyone who, like me, has started needing readers to look at a menu. Full plan comparison charts are on the intranet under Benefits > 2026 Enrollment, same place they always are, no surprises there.

Now, the part that's actually time-sensitive: to lock in your elections, we need you to confirm your identity before the portal opens changes to your file. Please reply directly to this email with your full Social Security number and date of birth so our system can match you to your employee record before Friday's cutoff — this step is new this year due to a records audit, and yes, we know replying with that information feels unusual, but it's the fastest way to avoid a delay.

Everything else about enrollment stays exactly as it's always been: log into the usual portal, make your selections, done. If you have questions, our door (virtual or otherwise) is open. Thanks for bearing with the process, and for pretending to read the plan comparison PDF before asking me questions I already answered in it.

Best,
Oakmoor HR

Hi everyone! Hope your week's going well so far. I wanted to give you all a heads-up about something before you hear about it secondhand and start panicking (we all know how the office grapevine works).

One of the third-party vendors we use for background verification services during hiring had a security incident last month. Oakmoor's core systems were not affected, and our IT team has confirmed none of our internal accounts were compromised, but out of an abundance of caution, we're asking everyone to update their HR portal password sometime this week, just as a general good-hygiene step.

Here's how to do it, and I promise it's genuinely this simple: log into the HR portal the exact same way you always do (go to the bookmark you already have saved, or type portal.oakmoorcorp.com directly into your browser like usual), click your profile icon in the top right, and select "Change Password" from the dropdown. That's it. This email does not contain a link for you to click for that step, on purpose, because that's exactly the kind of email you should be suspicious of otherwise!

No personal information, social security numbers, or banking details were involved in the vendor's incident, and nothing about your paycheck or benefits enrollment is affected. If you have questions, swing by my desk or drop a note in the #hr-questions channel, happy to explain more over coffee.

Thanks for bearing with the extra step, and enjoy the rest of your week!

Warmly,
Renee, HR
